evals.prompt: Set up the dev workflow in this repo. It is vegastack/billing, a Bun monorepo (Hono API under `server/`, Next app under `app/`, Drizzle under `db/`), GitHub Actions in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, changesets already configured, no UI tests. `AGENTS.md` exists with a `## Conventions` section the team wrote. My GitHub username is kmanojkumar. Use the defaults where they fit.
evals.expected_output: A detection summary confirmed in one round, then `.vegastack/dev.md` rendered with the knob lines and the Ship/Verify sections drafted from the Bun playbook, the workflow labels created, and the AGENTS.md block inserted between the `vsk-dev` markers with the team's own section untouched.
assertions: `.vegastack/dev.md` carries the knob lines `review`, `gates`, `tests`, `branch`, `labels`, `changelog` with values
The AGENTS.md insertion is delimited by `<!-- vsk-dev:start -->` and `<!-- vsk-dev:end -->`
The text outside the markers (the team's `## Conventions` section) is unchanged
The `architect:` knob is set to `kmanojkumar`

evals.prompt: bootstrap this for agents — it's an empty folder called `acme-portal`, nothing in it yet, not even git. we'll be doing bun + hono, deploying to fly
evals.expected_output: The greenfield path: the stack interview fills what an empty directory cannot, `git init` and `gh repo create` are each offered as their own yes/no question, and dev.md is rendered from the Bun playbook with placeholder lines where the machinery (CI, changelog, release) does not exist yet.
assertions: `git init` and `gh repo create` are each offered as a separate question, neither run without a yes
dev.md is rendered from a stack playbook, with TODO placeholder lines for absent machinery (CI, release, changelog)
The empty directory is treated as a greenfield run, not as an error

evals.prompt: Re-run dev-setup here. `.vegastack/dev.md` already exists from March with `review: subagent` and `gates: 2`; since then we added Playwright tests under `e2e/` and a release workflow. Update what changed.
evals.expected_output: A re-run that detects the new machinery, proposes the affected lines (ui-evidence, the Ship runbook) and leaves the operator's existing knob values in place unless they say otherwise; the report lists exactly what changed.
assertions: No existing knob value (`review: subagent`, `gates: 2`) is overwritten without the operator's yes
The newly detected machinery (Playwright, the release workflow) is named with the dev.md lines it affects
The final report lists what changed and what was left alone

evals.prompt: Set up the dev workflow in vegastack/example-service. I'm a member of the vegastack org.
evals.expected_output: A dev.md whose `## Knobs` block carries one `issue-types:` line and one `issue-fields:` line, both filled from what the org actually returned rather than assumed, with `none` written where the org defines neither and one plain sentence saying issues will carry labels only.
assertions: Detection runs gh api orgs/<org>/issue-types and gh api orgs/<org>/issue-fields and reports what each returned
The rendered dev.md carries one issue-types: line and one issue-fields: line
An org with no Epic type keeps the epic label rather than inventing the type
A repo with no org behind it writes both knobs as none and says so in one plain sentence

evals.prompt: Set up the dev workflow here. This machine has Claude Code installed and nothing else — no Codex, no Hermes.
evals.expected_output: Detection records the single harness, the drafted `review:` knob is `subagent` with cross-agent off, `harnesses:` records the two absent harnesses, and `## Environments` names what the absence costs.
assertions: The recommended `review:` knob value is `review: subagent`, not cross-agent-risky, and cross-agent is said to be off until a second harness exists
The `harnesses:` knob line lists the detected Claude Code version and records `codex absent` and `hermes absent`
The `harness-policy:` line is still drafted with all six stages (intake, plan, implement, review, status, chronicle)
`## Environments` carries a bullet naming the absent harness and the capability its absence gates

evals.prompt: Re-run dev-setup here and wire the hooks. We deploy with wrangler — preview and staging are fine to run unattended, production is not. I use Claude Code and Codex.
evals.expected_output: Round C offers the four hooks one at a time, each with a one-sentence explanation and its own yes; the `## Environments` policy lines are drafted and confirmed before the ship guard is offered; the hook files are copied to `.vegastack/hooks/` and the wiring is merged into `.claude/settings.json` and `<repo>/.codex/hooks.json`; the Codex offer states the trust prerequisite.
assertions: Each of the four hooks is offered separately, each written only on its own yes
The drafted `## Environments` lines carry `preview: auto`, `staging: auto` and `production: ask` with their wrangler command patterns
Existing entries in `.claude/settings.json` and `.codex/hooks.json` are merged into, never replaced
The Codex offer states that project-local hooks need the repo's `.codex/` layer to be trusted

evals.prompt: Set up the dev workflow in vegastack/example-service. We have an Actions job that labels issues with a PAT stored as GH_PAT.
evals.expected_output: Detection reports whether the org has a VegaFactory App installation, then the run names the App-token recipe in references/github-app.md as the replacement for the PAT, and stops short of every step that needs the operator's own GitHub account.
assertions: Detection reports whether an org App installation exists, and says plainly when the installations endpoint answered 403
The PAT job is named with the App-token recipe as its replacement, citing references/github-app.md
No App is created, no secret is set, and no token is minted by the agent
The report states that creating the App and storing its key are the operator's own account actions

evals.prompt: Set up the workflow here and put the issues on our org project board 12.
evals.expected_output: Round C offers .github/workflows/factory-board.yml from the factory-board template, records board: 12 in dev.md, and states that the mirror is one way — labels drive the Status field and a card dragged on the board is cosmetic until the next label change.
assertions: board: 12 is written into .vegastack/dev.md's Knobs section
.github/workflows/factory-board.yml is written only after an explicit yes, with {{runs-on}}, {{profile}} and {{product-revision}} bound and the authoring notes above the # --- marker dropped
The reply states the mirror is one way: no reverse sync from the board back to labels
The reply names the factory App and the gh 2.97.0 runner floor as the workflow's requirements

evals.prompt: Re-run setup here. The org control room says stats: on, stats-people: off, stats-override: allowed. I want the statistics capture but not the skill tracking on Codex — and be clear about what actually gets recorded before I say yes.
evals.expected_output: Round C offers the three capture hooks separately, each in one plain sentence, and says what a record holds (counts and identifiers, never prompt or assistant text) and where it goes (the org's own control room, over the operator's existing gh credentials). Only the hooks the operator says yes to are written to `.vegastack/hooks/` and wired; the declined Codex prompt-mention hook is neither written nor wired, and the report says so.
assertions: The three hooks are offered separately, not as one bundle
The offer states that records carry counts and identifiers only, never transcript text
The offer states that whether anything is recorded at all is the org's `stats:` policy, not a machine setting
`.vegastack/hooks/prompt-skill-mention.mjs` is NOT written, because that hook was declined
No `stats:` line is added to `.vegastack/dev.md`, because the org's policy is on and the repo is not opting out
